Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected()` fails because the formatted timezone string produced by FastDateFormat does not respect the timezone set on the Calendar instance passed to its format method. Instead, it always formats the timezone string according to the default timezone of the machine. The test compares the output from a correctly configured SimpleDateFormat (which uses the timezone from anotherZone) with the output from FastDateFormat (using the pattern "h:mma z") applied to a Calendar with anotherZone timezone. The difference arises because FastDateFormat.getInstance(pattern) is called without specifying a timezone, so it uses the default timezone internally for timezone formatting.

From the code snippets examined:

- FastDateFormat.getInstance(String) calls cache.getInstance(pattern, null, null), which defaults to the system default timezone (not the Calendar's timezone).
- The FastDateFormat.format(Calendar) method simply delegates to an internal printer's format method without consulting or overriding the Calendar's timezone when formatting the timezone portion of the pattern.
- The FormatCache.getInstance method creates instances of formatters keyed by pattern and timezone, but if no timezone is supplied, the default is used, leading to ignoring the Calendar timezone in formatting.
- There is no indication in these snippets that FastDateFormat's format method extracts and uses the timezone of the Calendar instance passed in to override the internally cached timezone.

Thus, the root cause is FastDateFormat's reliance on a cached internal timezone set at construction rather than dynamically switching to or respecting the timezone of Calendar instances passed to the format(Calendar) call. The "z" pattern (timezone string) is therefore always formatted with the default/cached timezone, ignoring the Calendar's timezone.

This explains why the test observes that while the time itself is adjusted correctly (the Calendar's time is correct), the timezone string printed is wrong (always the default timezone's name).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
